translations.idiomatic: The Grand Ancestor moved out to camp at Xinting and answered Youzhi in a letter, saying:

sentences.zh: 辱足下誚書，交道不終，爲恥已足。

translations.literal: I received your letter of reproach. That our friendship has not lasted is shame enough.
translations.idiomatic: I received your letter of reproach. That our friendship has not lasted is shame enough.

sentences.zh: 欲下便來，何故多罔君子。

translations.literal: If you wish to come down, then come; why so often wrong a gentleman?
translations.idiomatic: If you wish to come down, then come; why so often wrong a gentleman?

sentences.zh: 吾結髮入仕，豈期遠大，蓋感子路之言，每不擇官而宦。

translations.literal: From youth I entered service; how could I have expected great things? I was moved by Zilu's words and never chose office before serving.
translations.idiomatic: From youth I entered service; how could I have expected great things? I was moved by Zilu's words and never chose office before serving.

sentences.zh: 逮文帝之世，初被聖明鑒賞；

translations.literal: By Emperor Wen's time, I first received the sage and enlightened ruler's recognition and favor;
translations.idiomatic: By Emperor Wen's time, I first received the sage and enlightened ruler's recognition and favor;

sentences.zh: 及孝武之朝，復蒙英主顧眄。

translations.literal: and in Emperor Xiaowu's court, I again received the heroic ruler's regard.
translations.idiomatic: and in Emperor Xiaowu's court, I again received the heroic ruler's regard.

sentences.zh: 因此感激，未能自反。

translations.literal: Because of this I was moved with gratitude and could not turn back upon myself.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this I was moved with gratitude and could not turn back upon myself.

sentences.zh: 及與足下斂袂定交，款著分好，何嘗不勸慕古人國士之心，務重前良忠貞之節。

translations.literal: When I joined sleeves with you and fixed our friendship, our affection was clear and our bond distinct; did we ever fail to admire the hearts of ancient state heroes and prize the loyal integrity of former worthies?
translations.idiomatic: When I joined sleeves with you and fixed our friendship, our affection was clear and our bond distinct; did we ever fail to admire the hearts of ancient state heroes and prize the loyal integrity of former worthies?

sentences.zh: 至於契闊杯酒，殷勤攜袖，薦女成姻，志相然諾，義信之篤，誰與閒之。

translations.literal: As for our hard times and cups of wine, our earnest clasping of sleeves, my offering a daughter to make a marriage, and our wills pledging assent to each other, who could come between such deep duty and trust?
translations.idiomatic: As for our hard times and cups of wine, our earnest clasping of sleeves, my offering a daughter to make a marriage, and our wills pledging assent to each other, who could come between such deep duty and trust?

sentences.zh: 又乃景和陵虐，事切憂畏，明帝正位，運同休顯，啓臆論心，安危豈貳。

translations.literal: Then during Jinghe's oppressive cruelty, matters pressed us with fear and anxiety. When Emperor Ming took his proper place, our fortunes shared in his rest and splendor; opening our breasts and speaking our hearts, how could we differ in danger or safety?
translations.idiomatic: Then during Jinghe's oppressive cruelty, matters pressed us with fear and anxiety. When Emperor Ming took his proper place, our fortunes shared in his rest and splendor; opening our breasts and speaking our hearts, how could we differ in danger or safety?

sentences.zh: 元徽之季，聽高道慶邪言，欲相討伐，發威施敕，已行外內。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanhui, he listened to Gao Daoqing's crooked words and wished to attack us, issuing threats and edicts already carried out inside and outside the court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanhui, he listened to Gao Daoqing's crooked words and wished to attack us, issuing threats and edicts already carried out inside and outside the court.

sentences.zh: 于時臣子鉗口，道路以目。

translations.literal: At that time ministers and subjects clamped their mouths, and people on the roads spoke only with their eyes.
translations.idiomatic: At that time ministers and subjects clamped their mouths, and people on the roads spoke only with their eyes.

sentences.zh: 吾以分交義重，患難宜均，犯陵白刃，以相任保。

translations.literal: Because the duty of our shared friendship was weighty and hardship should be borne equally, I faced naked blades and guaranteed your safety.
translations.idiomatic: Because the duty of our shared friendship was weighty and hardship should be borne equally, I faced naked blades and guaranteed your safety.

sentences.zh: 悖主手敕，今封送相示。

translations.literal: The perverse ruler's handwritten edict is now sealed and sent for your inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The perverse ruler's handwritten edict is now sealed and sent for your inspection.

sentences.zh: 豈不畏威，念周旋之義耳。

translations.literal: Was I not afraid of his power? I simply thought of the duty by which we had moved together.
translations.idiomatic: Was I not afraid of his power? I simply thought of the duty by which we had moved together.

sentences.zh: 推此陰惠，何愧懷抱，不云足下猥含禍詖。

translations.literal: Considering this hidden favor, what shame is there in my breast? I did not say you vilely harbored calamitous deceit.
translations.idiomatic: Considering this hidden favor, what shame is there in my breast? I did not say you vilely harbored calamitous deceit.

sentences.zh: 前遣王思文所牒朝事，蓋情等家國，共詳衷否，虛心小大，必以先輸。

translations.literal: Earlier I sent Wang Siwen with a note on court affairs; my feeling was that family and state were alike, and that we should examine together whether the plan was sincere. With an empty heart, in great matters and small, I always laid my thoughts before you first.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier I sent Wang Siwen with a note on court affairs; my feeling was that family and state were alike, and that we should examine together whether the plan was sincere. With an empty heart, in great matters and small, I always laid my thoughts before you first.

sentences.zh: 問張雍州遷代之日，將欲誰擬？

translations.literal: I asked, when Zhang of Yongzhou was to be replaced, whom did you intend to propose?
translations.idiomatic: I asked, when Zhang of Yongzhou was to be replaced, whom did you intend to propose?

sentences.zh: 本是逆論來事，非欲代張，乃封此示張，激使見怒。

translations.literal: This was originally advance discussion of future affairs, not a wish to replace Zhang, yet you sealed it and showed it to Zhang, stirring him to anger.
translations.idiomatic: This was originally advance discussion of future affairs, not a wish to replace Zhang, yet you sealed it and showed it to Zhang, stirring him to anger.

sentences.zh: 若張惑一言，果興怨恨，事負雅素，君子所不可爲，況張之奉國，忠亮有本，情之見與，意契不貳邪？

translations.literal: If Zhang was misled by one phrase and truly became resentful, that betrayed our ordinary refinement and is something a gentleman would not do. Moreover, Zhang's service to the state has a foundation in loyalty and clarity, and his feeling toward me and his accord in intention are not divided.
translations.idiomatic: If Zhang was misled by one phrase and truly became resentful, that betrayed our ordinary refinement and is something a gentleman would not do. Moreover, Zhang's service to the state has a foundation in loyalty and clarity, and his feeling toward me and his accord in intention are not divided.

sentences.zh: 又張雍州啓事，稱彼中蠻動，兼民遭水患，敕令足下思經拯之計。

translations.literal: Again, Zhang of Yongzhou memorialized that the Man there were moving and that the people had also suffered flooding; an edict ordered you to consider plans to manage and rescue them.
translations.idiomatic: Again, Zhang of Yongzhou memorialized that the Man there were moving and that the people had also suffered flooding; an edict ordered you to consider plans to manage and rescue them.

sentences.zh: 吾亦有白，論國如家，布情而往，每思虛達。

translations.literal: I too had a statement: discussing the state as one would a family, I set out my feelings and sent them, always hoping for open understanding.
translations.idiomatic: I too had a statement: discussing the state as one would a family, I set out my feelings and sent them, always hoping for open understanding.

sentences.zh: 事之相接，恒必猜離。

translations.literal: Yet whenever matters touched each other, there was always suspicion and separation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever matters touched each other, there was always suspicion and separation.

sentences.zh: 反謂無故遣信，此乃覘察。

translations.literal: Instead you said that sending a messenger without cause was spying.
translations.idiomatic: Instead you said that sending a messenger without cause was spying.

sentences.zh: 平諒之襟，動則相阻，傷負心期，自誰作故？

translations.literal: A level and honest breast was obstructed whenever it moved; who caused this injury to the trust of our hearts?
translations.idiomatic: A level and honest breast was obstructed whenever it moved; who caused this injury to the trust of our hearts?

sentences.zh: 先時足下遣信，尋盟敦舊，厲以篤終，吾止附還白，申罄情本，契然遠要，方固金石。

translations.literal: Previously you sent a letter, seeking our covenant and strengthening old bonds, urging that we end with sincerity. I merely attached a reply, fully stating the root of my feelings, and our distant pledge was then firm as metal and stone.
translations.idiomatic: Previously you sent a letter, seeking our covenant and strengthening old bonds, urging that we end with sincerity. I merely attached a reply, fully stating the root of my feelings, and our distant pledge was then firm as metal and stone.

sentences.zh: 今日舉錯，定是誰恧久言邪？

translations.literal: In today's conduct, who is truly ashamed before those long-standing words?
translations.idiomatic: In today's conduct, who is truly ashamed before those long-standing words?

sentences.zh: 元徽末德，埶亡禋祀，足下備聞，無待亟述。

translations.literal: The failed virtue at the end of Yuanhui and the situation in which sacrifice was about to perish are things you fully heard; there is no need to repeat them urgently.
translations.idiomatic: The failed virtue at the end of Yuanhui and the situation in which sacrifice was about to perish are things you fully heard; there is no need to repeat them urgently.

sentences.zh: 太后惟憂，式遵前誥，興毀之略，事屬鄙躬。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager was anxious and followed the former command; the plan of raising up and casting down fell to my humble person.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager was anxious and followed the former command; the plan of raising up and casting down fell to my humble person.

sentences.zh: 黜昏樹明，實惟前則，寧宗靜國，何愧前脩。

translations.literal: Deposing darkness and establishing brightness truly followed former models; calming the clan and quieting the state, how did I shame earlier worthies?
translations.idiomatic: Deposing darkness and establishing brightness truly followed former models; calming the clan and quieting the state, how did I shame earlier worthies?

sentences.zh: 廢立有章，足下所允，冠弊之譏，將以何語？

translations.literal: Deposition and enthronement had proper order, and you approved it. With what words will you make the reproach about a worn-out cap?
translations.idiomatic: Deposition and enthronement had proper order, and you approved it. With what words will you make the reproach about a worn-out cap?

sentences.zh: 封爲郡王，寧爲失禮？

translations.literal: Was enfeoffing him as a commandery prince really a loss of ritual?
translations.idiomatic: Was enfeoffing him as a commandery prince really a loss of ritual?

sentences.zh: 景和無名，方之不愈乎？

translations.literal: Jinghe had no title; compared with that, was this not better?
translations.idiomatic: Jinghe had no title; compared with that, was this not better?

sentences.zh: 龍逢自匹夫之美，伊、霍則社稷之臣，同異相乘，非吾所受也。

translations.literal: Longfeng possessed the beauty of a common man, while Yi Yin and Huo Guang were ministers of the altars. To multiply sameness and difference together is not something I accept.
translations.idiomatic: Longfeng possessed the beauty of a common man, while Yi Yin and Huo Guang were ministers of the altars. To multiply sameness and difference together is not something I accept.

sentences.zh: 登齋有賞，壽寂已蒙之於前；

translations.literal: There were rewards for entering the chamber; Shouji had already received them before.
translations.idiomatic: There were rewards for entering the chamber; Shouji had already received them before.

sentences.zh: 同謀獲功，明皇亦行之於昔。

translations.literal: Those who shared the plan obtained merit; the Ming Emperor had also done this in the past.
translations.idiomatic: Those who shared the plan obtained merit; the Ming Emperor had also done this in the past.

sentences.zh: 此則接踵成事，誰敢異之。

translations.literal: These are accomplished precedents following one upon another; who would dare object?
translations.idiomatic: These are accomplished precedents following one upon another; who would dare object?

sentences.zh: 謂其大收宮女，劫奪天藏，器械金寶，必充私室。

translations.literal: You say that I made a great seizure of palace women, plundered the imperial stores, and surely filled my private rooms with weapons, gold, and treasure.
translations.idiomatic: You say that I made a great seizure of palace women, plundered the imperial stores, and surely filled my private rooms with weapons, gold, and treasure.

sentences.zh: 必若虛設市虎，亦可不翅此言；

translations.literal: If one falsely creates a tiger in the marketplace, it can be more than these words;
translations.idiomatic: If one falsely creates a tiger in the marketplace, it can be more than these words;

sentences.zh: 若以此詐民，天下豈患無眼。

translations.literal: but if this is used to deceive the people, need the realm fear it has no eyes?
translations.idiomatic: but if this is used to deceive the people, need the realm fear it has no eyes?

sentences.zh: 心苟無瑕，非所耿介。

translations.literal: If the heart has no flaw, this is not something to trouble over.
translations.idiomatic: If the heart has no flaw, this is not something to trouble over.

sentences.zh: 甲杖之授，事旣舊典，豈見有任鎮邦家，勳經定主，而可得出入輕單，不資寵衞！

translations.literal: The granting of armor and weapons is an old institution. Have you ever seen one entrusted with guarding the state and family, whose merit passed through settling the ruler, yet who could come and go lightly and alone, without relying on favored guards?
translations.idiomatic: The granting of armor and weapons is an old institution. Have you ever seen one entrusted with guarding the state and family, whose merit passed through settling the ruler, yet who could come and go lightly and alone, without relying on favored guards?

sentences.zh: 斯之患慮，豈直身憂。

translations.literal: This concern and anxiety was not merely worry for my own person.
translations.idiomatic: This concern and anxiety was not merely worry for my own person.

sentences.zh: 祗奉此恩，職惟事理。

translations.literal: Reverently receiving this favor, my duty lay only in the principle of the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Reverently receiving this favor, my duty lay only in the principle of the matter.

sentences.zh: 朱方之牧，公卿僉意，吾亦謂微勳之次，無忝一州。

translations.literal: The governorship of Zhufang was the unanimous view of the dukes and ministers; I too thought that, after my slight merit, I would not disgrace one province.
translations.idiomatic: The governorship of Zhufang was the unanimous view of the dukes and ministers; I too thought that, after my slight merit, I would not disgrace one province.

sentences.zh: 且魏、晉舊事，帝郷蕃職，何嘗豫州必曹，司州必馬？

translations.literal: Moreover, in the old affairs of Wei and Jin, when the imperial homeland was a provincial office, when did Yuzhou always have to be held by a Cao or Sizhou by a Sima?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the old affairs of Wei and Jin, when the imperial homeland was a provincial office, when did Yuzhou always have to be held by a Cao or Sizhou by a Sima?

sentences.zh: 折膠受柱，在體非愧。

translations.literal: Receiving the post as a bent glue support is no shame in substance.
translations.idiomatic: Receiving the post as a bent glue support is no shame in substance.

sentences.zh: 袁粲據石頭，足下無不可；

translations.literal: When Yuan Can held Shitou, you found nothing unacceptable;
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Can held Shitou, you found nothing unacceptable;

sentences.zh: 吾之守東府，來告便謂非。

translations.literal: but when I guarded the Eastern Office, your letter immediately called it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: but when I guarded the Eastern Office, your letter immediately called it wrong.

sentences.zh: 動容見疾，頻笑入戾，乃如是乎！

translations.literal: Every movement of my face is met with hatred, and repeated smiles are taken as crimes. Has it come to this?
translations.idiomatic: Every movement of my face is met with hatred, and repeated smiles are taken as crimes. Has it come to this?

sentences.zh: 袁粲、劉秉，受遇深重，家國旣安，不思撫鎮，遂與足下表裏潛規，據城之夜，豈顧社稷。

translations.literal: Yuan Can and Liu Bing had received deep and weighty treatment; once family and state were secure, they did not think to soothe and stabilize them, but instead secretly plotted with you inside and outside. On the night they occupied the city, how did they care for the altars?
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can and Liu Bing had received deep and weighty treatment; once family and state were secure, they did not think to soothe and stabilize them, but instead secretly plotted with you inside and outside. On the night they occupied the city, how did they care for the altars?

sentences.zh: 幸天未長亂，宗廟有靈，卽與褚衞軍協謀義斷，以時殄滅。

translations.literal: Fortunately Heaven did not prolong the disorder, and the ancestral temple had spirit; I immediately joined plans with Chu, General of the Guard, made a righteous decision, and destroyed them in time.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately Heaven did not prolong the disorder, and the ancestral temple had spirit; I immediately joined plans with Chu, General of the Guard, made a righteous decision, and destroyed them in time.

sentences.zh: 想足下聞之，悵然孤沮。

translations.literal: I imagine that when you heard of it, you were disappointed, isolated, and dejected.
translations.idiomatic: I imagine that when you heard of it, you were disappointed, isolated, and dejected.

sentences.zh: 小兒忝侍中，代來之澤，遇直上臺，便呼一家兩錄。

translations.literal: My young son shamefully held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary, a grace passed down through generations; when he happened to serve on duty in the upper offices, you immediately called it one family holding two recorderships.
translations.idiomatic: My young son shamefully held the post of Attendant-in-Ordinary, a grace passed down through generations; when he happened to serve on duty in the upper offices, you immediately called it one family holding two recorderships.

sentences.zh: 發不擇言，良以太甚。

translations.literal: You spoke without choosing your words; truly this was excessive.
translations.idiomatic: You spoke without choosing your words; truly this was excessive.

sentences.zh: 吾之方寸，古列共言，乃以陶、庾往賢，大見譏責，足下自省，詎得以此見貽邪？

translations.literal: My heart is something men of old have all spoken of, yet you use former worthies such as Tao and Yu to reproach me greatly. Examine yourself: how could you present me with this?
translations.idiomatic: My heart is something men of old have all spoken of, yet you use former worthies such as Tao and Yu to reproach me greatly. Examine yourself: how could you present me with this?

sentences.zh: 比蹤夷、叔，論吾則可，行過桀、蹠，無乃近誣哉！

translations.literal: To compare my tracks with Boyi and Shuqi may be acceptable when speaking of me; to say my conduct surpasses Jie and Zhi is surely close to slander.
translations.idiomatic: To compare my tracks with Boyi and Shuqi may be acceptable when speaking of me; to say my conduct surpasses Jie and Zhi is surely close to slander.

sentences.zh: 謂吾不朝，此則良誨，朝之與否，想更問之。

translations.literal: You say I did not attend court; this is good instruction. As to whether I attended or not, I expect you should ask again.
translations.idiomatic: You say I did not attend court; this is good instruction. As to whether I attended or not, I expect you should ask again.

sentences.zh: 足下受先帝之恩施，擁戎西州，鼎湖之日，率土載奔，而宴安中流，酣飲自若，卽懷狼望，陵侮皇朝。

translations.literal: You received the Former Emperor's grace and held troops in the western province. On the day of Dinghu, all the land rushed in mourning, yet you feasted at ease in midstream and drank heavily as if nothing had happened, already harboring a wolf's ambition and insulting the imperial court.
translations.idiomatic: You received the Former Emperor's grace and held troops in the western province. On the day of Dinghu, all the land rushed in mourning, yet you feasted at ease in midstream and drank heavily as if nothing had happened, already harboring a wolf's ambition and insulting the imperial court.

sentences.zh: 晉熙殿下，以皇弟代鎮，而斷割候迎，罔蔑宗子，驅略士馬，悉以西上，郢中所遺，僅餘劣弱。

translations.literal: His Highness of Jinxi, as the emperor's younger brother, went to replace you in the command, but you cut off the welcoming parties, slighted the imperial kinsman, drove off and seized soldiers and horses, and sent them all westward, leaving in Ying only the inferior and weak.
translations.idiomatic: His Highness of Jinxi, as the emperor's younger brother, went to replace you in the command, but you cut off the welcoming parties, slighted the imperial kinsman, drove off and seized soldiers and horses, and sent them all westward, leaving in Ying only the inferior and weak.

sentences.zh: 昔徵茅不入，猶動義師；

translations.literal: In the past, when tribute grass was not sent in, righteous armies were still mobilized;
translations.idiomatic: In the past, when tribute grass was not sent in, righteous armies were still mobilized;

sentences.zh: 況荊州物產，雍、崏、交、梁之會，自足下爲牧，薦獻何品？

translations.literal: how much more when Jingzhou, with its products and its meeting point with Yong, Min, Jiao, and Liang, has offered what goods since you became its governor?
translations.idiomatic: how much more when Jingzhou, with its products and its meeting point with Yong, Min, Jiao, and Liang, has offered what goods since you became its governor?

sentences.zh: 良馬勁卒，彼中不無，良皮美罽，商賂所聚，前後貢奉，多少何如？

translations.literal: Fine horses and strong soldiers are not lacking there; good hides and beautiful rugs gather through trade and gifts. How much tribute has been offered before and after?
translations.idiomatic: Fine horses and strong soldiers are not lacking there; good hides and beautiful rugs gather through trade and gifts. How much tribute has been offered before and after?

sentences.zh: 唯聞太官時納飲食耳。

translations.literal: I have heard only that food has sometimes been sent to the Grand Provisioner.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard only that food has sometimes been sent to the Grand Provisioner.

sentences.zh: 桂陽之難，坐觀成敗，自以雍容漢南，西伯可擬。

translations.literal: During the Guiyang crisis, you sat watching success or failure, considering yourself so composed south of the Han that you could be compared to the Earl of the West.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guiyang crisis, you sat watching success or failure, considering yourself so composed south of the Han that you could be compared to the Earl of the West.

sentences.zh: 賴原卽天世，非望亦消。

translations.literal: Thanks to the fact that Yuan soon died, your improper hopes also vanished.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to the fact that Yuan soon died, your improper hopes also vanished.

sentences.zh: 又招集逋亡，斷遏行侶，治舟試艦，恒以朝廷爲旗的，秣馬桉劔，常願天下有風塵，爲人臣者，固若是邪！

translations.literal: You also gathered fugitives, cut off travelers, repaired boats and tested warships, constantly took the court as your target, fed horses and gripped your sword, and always wished for dust storms under Heaven. Is this truly how a subject acts?
translations.idiomatic: You also gathered fugitives, cut off travelers, repaired boats and tested warships, constantly took the court as your target, fed horses and gripped your sword, and always wished for dust storms under Heaven. Is this truly how a subject acts?

sentences.zh: 至乃不遵制書，敕下如空，國恩莫行，命令擁隔，詔除郡縣，輙自板代，罷官去職，禁還京師。

translations.literal: You even failed to obey imperial documents, treated edicts as empty, blocked the state's grace from being carried out, obstructed commands, replaced appointments to commanderies and counties with your own temporary commissions, and forbade dismissed officials returning to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: You even failed to obey imperial documents, treated edicts as empty, blocked the state's grace from being carried out, obstructed commands, replaced appointments to commanderies and counties with your own temporary commissions, and forbade dismissed officials returning to the capital.

sentences.zh: 凶人出境，無不千里尋躡，而反募臺將，來必厚加給賞。

translations.literal: When wicked men left your territory, you always pursued them a thousand li, yet you recruited generals from the court, richly rewarding any who came.
translations.idiomatic: When wicked men left your territory, you always pursued them a thousand li, yet you recruited generals from the court, richly rewarding any who came.

sentences.zh: 太妃遣使市馬，齎寶往蜀，足下悉皆斷折，以爲私財，此皆遠邇共聞，暴於視聽。

translations.literal: When the Grand Consort sent envoys to buy horses and carry valuables to Shu, you cut them all off and took them as private wealth. All this has been heard far and near and is exposed to sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Consort sent envoys to buy horses and carry valuables to Shu, you cut them all off and took them as private wealth. All this has been heard far and near and is exposed to sight and hearing.

sentences.zh: 主上叡明當璧，宇縣同慶，絕域奉贄，萬國通書，而盤桓百日，始有單騎，事存送往，於此可徵。

translations.literal: When the sovereign, in his brilliant wisdom, held the jade disk, the realm rejoiced together, distant lands offered gifts, and ten thousand states sent letters; yet you lingered a hundred days before there was even a single rider. That your intent lay merely in seeing off the past can be proven from this.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign, in his brilliant wisdom, held the jade disk, the realm rejoiced together, distant lands offered gifts, and ten thousand states sent letters; yet you lingered a hundred days before there was even a single rider. That your intent lay merely in seeing off the past can be proven from this.

sentences.zh: 不朝如此，誰應受誚？

translations.literal: With nonattendance like this, who should receive reproach?
translations.idiomatic: With nonattendance like this, who should receive reproach?

sentences.zh: 反以見呵，非所反側。

translations.literal: For you instead to scold me is not something I can rest easy with.
translations.idiomatic: For you instead to scold me is not something I can rest easy with.

sentences.zh: 今乃勒兵以闚象館，長戟以指魏闕，不亦爲忠臣孝子之所痛心疾首邪？

translations.literal: Now you marshal troops to peer into the Elephant Hall and point long halberds at the palace gates. Is this not something to make loyal ministers and filial sons grieve in heart and ache in head?
translations.idiomatic: Now you marshal troops to peer into the Elephant Hall and point long halberds at the palace gates. Is this not something to make loyal ministers and filial sons grieve in heart and ache in head?

sentences.zh: 賢子元琰獲免虎口，及凌波西邁，吾所發遣。

translations.literal: Your worthy son Yuanyan escaped the tiger's mouth, and when he crossed the waves westward, I was the one who sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Your worthy son Yuanyan escaped the tiger's mouth, and when he crossed the waves westward, I was the one who sent him off.

sentences.zh: 猶推素懷，不畏嗤嗤。

translations.literal: I still extended my old feelings and did not fear ridicule.
translations.idiomatic: I still extended my old feelings and did not fear ridicule.

sentences.zh: 足下尚復滅君臣之紀，況吾布衣之交乎？

translations.literal: Yet you still destroy the order between ruler and subject; how much more my common-cloth friendship with you?
translations.idiomatic: Yet you still destroy the order between ruler and subject; how much more my common-cloth friendship with you?

sentences.zh: 遂事不諫，旣往難咎。

translations.literal: What is already done cannot be remonstrated against, and what is past is hard to blame.
translations.idiomatic: What is already done cannot be remonstrated against, and what is past is hard to blame.

sentences.zh: 今六師西向，爲足下憂之。

translations.literal: Now the six armies face west, and I worry for you.
translations.idiomatic: Now the six armies face west, and I worry for you.

sentences.zh: 攸之與兼長史江乂、別駕傅宣等守江陵城。

translations.literal: Youzhi, with acting chief clerk Jiang Yi and registrar Fu Xuan and others, held Jiangling city.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi, with acting chief clerk Jiang Yi, registrar Fu Xuan, and the rest, held Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒軍中力授，因以爲別。

translations.literal: They judged Jinger's army weak in strength and therefore treated it as a side matter.
translations.idiomatic: They thought Jinger's host too slight to matter and set it aside.

sentences.zh: 敬兒告變使至，太祖大喜，進號鎮軍將軍，加散騎常侍，改爲都督，給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: When Jinger's messenger reporting the turn of affairs arrived, the Grand Ancestor rejoiced greatly; Jinger was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Army, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, changed to overall commander, and granted one suite of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinger's messenger came with word of the betrayal, the Grand Ancestor was overjoyed; Jinger was raised to General Who Pacifies the Army, made Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders, named overall commander, and given a suite of martial music.

sentences.zh: 攸之於郢城敗走，其子元琰與兼長史江乂、別駕傅宣等守江陵城。

translations.literal: Youzhi was routed and fled from Ying; his son Yuan Yan, with acting chief clerk Jiang Yi, registrar Fu Xuan, and others, held Jiangling city.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi was broken at Ying and fled; his son Yuan Yan, with Jiang Yi, Fu Xuan, and the rest, still held Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 敬兒軍至白水，元琰聞城外鶴唳，謂是呌聲，心懼欲走。

translations.literal: When Jinger's army reached White Water, Yuan Yan heard cranes crying outside the walls, took it for shouting, and in fear meant to run.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger's army came to White Water; Yuan Yan heard cranes beyond the wall and mistook them for battle cries—his heart failed and he meant to bolt.

sentences.zh: 其夜，乂、宣開門出奔，城潰，元琰奔寵洲，見殺。

translations.literal: That night Yi and Xuan opened the gates and fled; the city collapsed; Yuan Yan fled to Chong Isle and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: That night Jiang Yi and Fu Xuan opened the gates and ran; the defenses gave way; Yuan Yan fled to Chong Isle and was slain.

sentences.zh: 百姓旣相抄敓，敬兒至江陵，誅攸之親黨，沒入其財物數十萬，悉以入私。

translations.literal: The people were already looting one another; when Jinger reached Jiangling he executed Youzhi's kin and partisans, confiscated his goods to the sum of several hundred thousand, and put it all to private use.
translations.idiomatic: The people were already tearing at one another; when Jinger entered Jiangling he killed Youzhi's kin and allies, seized goods worth several hundred thousand, and kept every coin for himself.

sentences.zh: 攸之於湯渚村自經死，居民送首荊州，敬兒使楯擎之，蓋以青繖，徇諸市郭，乃送京師。

translations.literal: Youzhi hanged himself at Tangzhu village; the inhabitants sent his head to Jing province; Jinger had it borne on a shield, covered with a green canopy, paraded through the market wards, and then sent it to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhi hanged himself at Tangzhu village; the locals sent his head to Jing; Jinger had it carried on a shield under a green canopy, displayed through the wards, and then forwarded to the capital.

sentences.zh: 進號征西將軍，爵爲公，增邑爲四千戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to General Who Pacifies the West, enfeoffed as duke, and his fief was raised to four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to General Who Pacifies the West, made duke, and his fief increased to four thousand households.

sentences.zh: 敬兒於襄陽城西起宅，聚財貨。

translations.literal: Jinger built a mansion west of Xiangyang city and heaped up wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger raised a great house west of Xiangyang and piled up treasure.

sentences.zh: 又欲移羊叔子墮淚碑，於其處立臺，綱紀諫曰：「羊太傅遺德，不宜遷動。」

translations.literal: He also wished to move Yang Hu's Weeping Stele and set up a terrace in its place; his steward remonstrated: "The Grand Tutor Yang's lingering virtue ought not to be disturbed."
translations.idiomatic: He also meant to shift Yang Hu's Weeping Stele and build a terrace where it stood; his steward pleaded, "Grand Tutor Yang's grace still lingers here—it should not be moved."

sentences.zh: 敬兒曰：「太傅是誰？

translations.literal: Jinger said: "Who is this Grand Tutor?
translations.idiomatic: Jinger said, "Grand Tutor? Who is that?

sentences.zh: 我不識也。」

translations.literal: I do not know him."
translations.idiomatic: I never heard of him."

sentences.zh: 敬兒弟恭兒，不肯出官，常居上保村中，與居民不異。

translations.literal: Jinger's younger brother Gong'er would not take office and always lived in Shangbao village like any common villager.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger's younger brother Gong'er refused office and lived in Shangbao village no differently from the neighbors.

sentences.zh: 敬兒呼納之甚厚，恭兒月一出視敬兒，輙復去。

translations.literal: Jinger summoned him and treated him very generously; Gong'er came once a month to see Jinger and then left again.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger called him in and lavished gifts on him; Gong'er came once a month to visit and always went home again.

sentences.zh: 恭兒本名豬兒，隨敬兒改名也。

translations.literal: Gong'er's original name was Zhuer; he changed it when he followed Jinger.
translations.idiomatic: Gong'er had been named Zhuer and changed his name when he followed Jinger.

sentences.zh: 初，敬兒旣斬沈攸之，使報隨郡太守劉道宗，聚衆得千餘人，立營頓。

translations.literal: Earlier, after Jinger had beheaded Shen Youzhi, he sent word to Suixian Administrator Liu Daozong; Daozong gathered more than a thousand men and pitched a camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinger first struck down Shen Youzhi, he reported to Suixian Administrator Liu Daozong; Daozong mustered more than a thousand men and made camp.

sentences.zh: 司州刺史姚道和不殺攸之使，密令道宗罷軍。

translations.literal: Sizhou Inspector Yao Daohe did not kill Youzhi's envoy but secretly ordered Daozong to disband his force.
translations.idiomatic: Sizhou Inspector Yao Daohe spared Youzhi's envoy and secretly told Daozong to stand his men down.

sentences.zh: 及攸之圍郢，道和遣軍頓堇城爲郢援，事平，依例蒙爵賞。

translations.literal: When Youzhi besieged Ying, Daohe sent troops to camp at Jincheng as relief for Ying; when the affair was settled he received rank and reward by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Youzhi besieged Ying, Daohe sent a column to hold Jincheng in Ying's aid; when the war ended he took honors and reward like the rest.

sentences.zh: 敬兒具以啓聞，

translations.literal: Jinger laid the whole matter out in a memorial,
translations.idiomatic: Jinger laid the whole matter before the throne.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，太祖令有司奏道和罪，誅之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Grand Ancestor ordered the relevant offices to memorialize Daohe's crime, and he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Grand Ancestor ordered the offices to indict Daohe, and he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 道和字敬邕，羌主姚興孫也。

translations.literal: Daohe, styled Jingyong, was a grandson of the Di ruler Yao Xing.
translations.idiomatic: Daohe, styled Jingyong, was grandson to the Di king Yao Xing.

sentences.zh: 父萬壽，偽鎮東大將軍，降宋武帝，卒於散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Wanshou was a false Grand General Who Pacifies the East and surrendered to Emperor Wu of Song; he died as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wanshou had been a puppet Grand General Who Pacifies the East, surrendered to Emperor Wu of Song, and died as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Scattered Riders.

sentences.zh: 道和出身爲孝武安北行佐，有世名，頗讀書史。

translations.literal: Daohe first entered service as acting staff on the Pacifying North campaign of Emperor Xiaowu and had a family name; he read histories with some care.
translations.idiomatic: Daohe first served as acting staff on Emperor Xiaowu's Pacifying North campaign, came of a great house, and read widely in the histories.

sentences.zh: 常誑人云：「祖天子，父天子，身經作皇太子。」

translations.literal: He would often boast to people: "My grandfather was Son of Heaven, my father was Son of Heaven, and I myself was once nearly made crown prince."
translations.idiomatic: He loved to brag: "Grandfather was Son of Heaven, father was Son of Heaven, and I myself was once within a breath of the crown prince."

sentences.zh: 元徽中爲游擊將軍，隨太祖新亭破桂陽賊有功，爲撫軍司馬，出爲司州，疑怯無斷，故及於誅。

translations.literal: In the Yuanhui era he was General of the Rapid Attack and, with the Grand Ancestor at Xinting, helped break the Guiyang rebels and had merit; he became Chief Aide of the Pacifying Army, went out as inspector of Sizhou, and, being suspicious and timid and without resolve, came to execution.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhui he was General of the Rapid Attack; at Xinting with the Grand Ancestor he helped crush the Guiyang rebels and won merit, became Chief Aide of the Pacifying Army, and went out as inspector of Sizhou—but doubt and timidity left him without judgment, and that brought him to the axe.

sentences.zh: 三年，徵敬兒爲護軍將軍，常侍如故。

translations.literal: In the third year Jinger was summoned as General of the Protecting Army, with Regular Attendant as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Jinger was called in as General of the Protecting Army, Regular Attendant as before.

sentences.zh: 敬兒武將，不習朝儀，聞當內遷，乃於密室中屏人學揖讓答對，空中俯仰，如此竟日，妾侍竊窺笑焉。

translations.literal: Jinger was a military man and did not know court ritual; hearing he was to move inward, he shut himself in a private room, dismissed attendants, and practiced bowing, yielding, and replies to questions, bowing up and down to empty air all day—his concubines peeked in and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Jinger was a soldier and knew nothing of court forms; when he heard he was to enter the capital, he cleared a inner room, sent everyone out, and rehearsed bows, steps, and answers to the throne, bobbing at the empty air all day while his women stole looks and laughed.

sentences.zh: 太祖卽位，授侍中，中軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, Jinger was made Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor took the throne, Jinger was made Palace Attendant and General of the Central Army.

sentences.zh: 以敬兒秩窮五等，一仍前封，

translations.literal: Because Jinger's rank had reached the fifth degree of nobility, his former enfeoffment was left unchanged,
translations.idiomatic: Jinger's rank had already touched the fifth degree of nobility, so his old fief was left as it was.

sentences.zh: 建元二年，遷散騎常侍，車騎將軍，置佐史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianyuan, he was moved to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and General of the Flying Cavalry, with staff appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianyuan, soon he was shifted to Regular Attendant of the Scattered Riders and General of the Flying Cavalry, with a full staff.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，敬兒於家竊泣曰：「官家大老天子，可惜！

translations.literal: When the Grand Ancestor died, Jinger wept in private at home and said: "The August One is gone—the Son of Heaven is lost, what a pity!
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Ancestor died, Jinger wept at home and said, "The old emperor is gone—what a pity for the Son of Heaven!

sentences.zh: 太子年少，向我所不及也。」

translations.literal: The crown prince is young; he will not reach what I had from him."
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince is young; he will never favor me as the old man did."

sentences.zh: 遺詔加敬兒開府儀同三司，將拜，謂其妓妾曰：「我拜後，應開黃閤。」

translations.literal: The testamentary edict advanced Jinger to Defender of the State with ritual parity of the Three Excellencies; as he was about to receive the appointment he told his concubines: "After I am appointed, the Yellow Gate ought to open."
translations.idiomatic: The testamentary edict made him Defender of the State with ritual parity of the Three Excellencies; on the eve of the audience he told his women, "Once I take the seal, the Yellow Gate should swing wide."

sentences.zh: 因口自爲鼓聲。

translations.literal: He thereupon beat a drum rhythm with his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: And he beat a drum pattern with his mouth.

sentences.zh: 旣拜，王敬則戲之，呼爲褚淵。

translations.literal: After the appointment Wang Jingze teased him and called him Chu Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites Wang Jingze mocked him and hailed him as Chu Yuan.

sentences.zh: 敬兒曰：「我馬上所得，終不能作華林閤勳也。」

translations.literal: Jinger said: "What I won from horseback will never make me a Huailin Pavilion merit noble."
translations.idiomatic: Jinger said, "What I won in the saddle will never turn me into one of those Huailin Pavilion courtiers."

sentences.zh: 敬則甚恨。

translations.literal: Jingze hated him deeply for it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingze hated him for it from that day on.

sentences.zh: 敬兒始不識書，晚旣爲方伯，乃習學讀《孝經》《論語》。

translations.literal: Jing'er at first could not read; only late, once he had become a regional governor, did he study and read the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er began illiterate; not until he was a regional governor did he take up study and read the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 於新林慈姥廟爲妾乞兒祝神，自稱三公。

translations.literal: At the Cimu Shrine at Xinlin he had a concubine beg as a mendicant to pray to the god, calling herself one of the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: At the Cimu Shrine in Xinlin he sent a concubine to beg alms and pray to the spirit, styling herself a member of the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 然而意知滿足，初得鼓吹，羞便奏之。

translations.literal: Yet he knew when he had enough; when he first received the military wind-and-percussion guard, he was ashamed even to have it played.
translations.idiomatic: He knew, though, when he had enough; the first time he was granted martial drums and pipes, he was too ashamed to let them sound.

sentences.zh: 初娶前妻毛氏，生子道文。

translations.literal: He first married his first wife, the Lady Mao; she bore Daowen.
translations.idiomatic: His first marriage was to the Lady Mao; she bore Daowen.

sentences.zh: 後娶尚氏，尚氏有美色，敬兒棄前妻而納之。

translations.literal: Later he married the Lady Shang; she was beautiful, and Jing'er abandoned his first wife to take her.
translations.idiomatic: Later he married the Lady Shang, who was beautiful; Jing'er cast off his first wife and brought her in.

sentences.zh: 尚氏猶居襄陽宅不自隨，敬兒慮不復外出，乃迎家口悉下至都。

translations.literal: Lady Shang still lived at the house in Xiangyang and would not accompany him; fearing he would never go out again, he brought his entire household down to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Shang stayed in the Xiangyang house and would not follow; afraid he would never leave the capital again, he moved the whole household down to court.

sentences.zh: 啓世祖，不蒙勞問，敬兒心疑。

translations.literal: He memorialized Emperor Shizu but received no courteous inquiry in return; Jing'er grew suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized Emperor Shizu and won no gracious reply; Jing'er's heart turned doubtful.

sentences.zh: 及垣崇祖死，愈恐懼，妻謂敬兒曰：「昔時夢手熱如火，而君得南陽郡。

translations.literal: When Yuan Chongzu died his fear deepened. His wife said to Jing'er: "Once I dreamed my hand burned like fire, and you received Nanyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Chongzu died his terror mounted. His wife told Jing'er: "Long ago I dreamed my hand burned like fire, and you won Nanyang commandery.

sentences.zh: 元徽中，夢半身熱，而君得本州。

translations.literal: In the Yuangui era I dreamed half my body burned, and you received this province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuangui years I dreamed half my body burned, and you won this province.

sentences.zh: 今復夢舉體熱矣。」

translations.literal: Now again I dream my whole body burns."
translations.idiomatic: Now I dream my whole body burns again."

sentences.zh: 有閹人聞其言，說之。

translations.literal: A eunuch overheard her words and reported them.
translations.idiomatic: A palace eunuch heard her and told others.

sentences.zh: 事達世祖。

translations.literal: The matter reached Emperor Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Emperor Shizu.

sentences.zh: 敬兒又遣使與蠻中交關，世祖疑其有異志，

translations.literal: Jing'er also sent envoys to deal with the southern barbarians; Shizu suspected disloyal intent,
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er also sent envoys to traffic with the southern barbarians; Shizu suspected treason in his heart.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，敕朝臣華林八關齋，於坐收敬兒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, he ordered the court to the Hualin Eight Precepts assembly and seized Jing'er in his seat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming, he ordered the court to the Hualin Eight Precepts fast and took Jing'er in his seat.

sentences.zh: 敬兒左右雷仲顯知有變，抱敬兒而泣。

translations.literal: Jing'er's attendant Lei Zhongxian sensed trouble, embraced Jing'er, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er's attendant Lei Zhongxian knew something was wrong, held Jing'er, and wept.

sentences.zh: 敬兒脫冠貂投地曰：「用此物誤我。」

translations.literal: Jing'er tore off his sable cap and threw it to the ground, saying: "This thing ruined me."
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er stripped off his sable cap and flung it down, saying: "This is what destroyed me."

sentences.zh: 少日，伏誅。

translations.literal: A few days later he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he was put to death.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：

translations.literal: Edict:
translations.idiomatic: The edict read:

sentences.zh: 敬兒蠢茲邊裔，昏迷不脩。

translations.literal: Jing'er was stupid, from this border stock, benighted and uncultivated.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er was stupid, from this border stock, benighted and uncultivated.

sentences.zh: 屬值宋季多難，頗獲野戰之力。

translations.literal: He happened to meet the many troubles at the end of Song and gained some credit for fighting in the field.
translations.idiomatic: He happened to meet the many troubles at the end of Song and gained some credit for fighting in the field.

sentences.zh: 拔迹行伍，超登非分。

translations.literal: He rose from the ranks and leapt beyond his proper station.
translations.idiomatic: He rose from the ranks and leapt beyond his proper station.

sentences.zh: 而愚躁無已，矜伐滋深。

translations.literal: Yet his foolish rashness never ceased, and his boasting and self-praise grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his foolish rashness never ceased, and his boasting and self-praise grew deeper.

sentences.zh: 往莅本州，久苞異志。

translations.literal: When he formerly governed his home province, he had long harbored disloyal intentions.
translations.idiomatic: When he formerly governed his home province, he had long harbored disloyal intentions.

sentences.zh: 在昔含弘，庶能懲革。

translations.literal: In the past We showed broad forbearance, hoping he might be chastened and reform.
translations.idiomatic: In the past We showed broad forbearance, hoping he might be chastened and reform.

sentences.zh: 位班三槐，秩窮五等，懷音靡聞，奸回屢構。

translations.literal: His rank stood among the Three Excellencies and his noble grade reached the highest of the five orders, yet no sound of gratitude was heard, and treacherous perversity was repeatedly formed.
translations.idiomatic: His rank stood among the Three Excellencies and his noble grade reached the highest of the five orders, yet no sound of gratitude was heard, and treacherous perversity was repeatedly formed.

sentences.zh: 去歲迄今，嫌貳滋甚。

translations.literal: From last year to now, suspicion and duplicity have grown ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: From last year to now, suspicion and duplicity have grown ever worse.

sentences.zh: 鎮東將軍敬則、丹陽尹安民每侍接之日，陳其凶狡，必圖反噬。

translations.literal: General Who Guards the East Jingze and Yin Anmin of Danyang, whenever they attended and met with Us, stated that he was vicious and crafty and would surely plot to bite back.
translations.idiomatic: General Who Guards the East Jingze and Yin Anmin of Danyang, whenever they attended and met with Us, stated that he was vicious and crafty and would surely plot to bite back.

sentences.zh: 朕猶謂恩義所感，本質可移。

translations.literal: We still thought that moved by grace and duty, his basic nature might change.
translations.idiomatic: We still thought that moved by grace and duty, his basic nature might change.

sentences.zh: 頃者已來，釁戾遂著，自以子弟在西，足動殊俗，招扇羣蠻，規擾樊、夏。

translations.literal: Recently, however, his offenses and perversity became manifest. Thinking his sons and younger kinsmen in the west were enough to stir alien peoples, he summoned and incited the various Man, scheming to disturb Fan and Xia.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, however, his offenses and perversity became manifest. Thinking his sons and younger kinsmen in the west were enough to stir alien peoples, he summoned and incited the various Man, scheming to disturb Fan and Xia.

sentences.zh: 假託妖巫，用相震惑，妄設徵祥，潛圖問鼎。

translations.literal: He falsely relied on shamans and witches to frighten and delude them, fabricated portents and auspicious signs, and secretly plotted to ask after the tripods.
translations.idiomatic: He falsely relied on shamans and witches to frighten and delude them, fabricated portents and auspicious signs, and secretly plotted to ask after the tripods.

sentences.zh: 履霜於開運之辰，堅冰於嗣業之世，此而可忍，孰不可容！

translations.literal: He trod frost in the hour when fortune opened, and hard ice formed in the age that inherited the enterprise. If this can be tolerated, what cannot be endured?
translations.idiomatic: He trod frost in the hour when fortune opened, and hard ice formed in the age that inherited the enterprise. If this can be tolerated, what cannot be endured?

sentences.zh: 天道禍淫，逆謀顯露。

translations.literal: The Way of Heaven brings disaster on excess, and his rebellious plot has been exposed.
translations.idiomatic: The Way of Heaven brings disaster on excess, and his rebellious plot has been exposed.

sentences.zh: 建康民湯天獲商行入蠻，備睹姦計，信驛書翰，證驗炳明。

translations.literal: Tang Tianhuo, a commoner of Jiankang, traveled among the Man for trade and fully saw the treacherous plan; courier letters and written messages make the proof brilliantly clear.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Tianhuo, a commoner of Jiankang, traveled among the Man for trade and fully saw the treacherous plan; courier letters and written messages make the proof brilliantly clear.

sentences.zh: 便可收掩，式正刑辟；同黨所及，特皆原宥。

translations.literal: He may therefore be arrested at once, to set punishments and laws right; as for those reached as his associates, all are specially pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: He may therefore be arrested at once, to set punishments and laws right; as for those reached as his associates, all are specially pardoned.

sentences.zh: 子道文，武陵內史，道暢，征虜功曹，道固弟道休，竝伏誅。

translations.literal: His sons Daowen, Administrator of Wuling; Daochang, registrar on the staff of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians; and Daogu's younger brother Daoxiu were all executed.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Daowen, administrator of Wuling; Daochang, registrar on the staff of the General Who Punishes the Barbarians; and Daogu's younger brother Daoxiu were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 少子道慶，見宥。

translations.literal: The youngest son, Daoqing, was spared.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest son, Daoqing, was pardoned.

sentences.zh: 後數年，上與豫章王嶷三日曲水內宴，舴艋船流至御坐前覆沒，上由是言及敬兒，悔殺之。

translations.literal: Years later, at the third-day spring banquet on the winding waters, a punt drifted to the imperial seat and capsized; the emperor spoke of Jing'er and regretted killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Years on, at the third-day spring banquet by the winding stream, a skiff drifted to the throne and sank; the emperor spoke of Jing'er and rued having killed him.

sentences.zh: 恭兒官至員外郎。

translations.literal: Gong'er rose to Outer Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Gong'er reached the post of Outer Attendant.

sentences.zh: 在襄陽，聞敬兒敗，將數十騎走入蠻中，收捕不得。

translations.literal: At Xiangyang, hearing of Jing'er's fall, he took several dozen riders and fled into the barbarian lands; pursuit could not catch him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xiangyang, when he heard Jing'er had fallen, he rode off with several dozen followers into the barbarian hills; hunters could not take him.

sentences.zh: 後首出，上原其罪。

translations.literal: Later he surrendered himself; the emperor pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he came forward of his own accord; the emperor forgave his crime.

sentences.zh: 【史論】

translations.literal: Historical appraisal
translations.idiomatic: Historical appraisal

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：平世武臣，立身有術，若非愚以取信，則宜智以自免，心迹無阻，乃見優容。

translations.literal: The historian writes: In peaceful times a martial officer who would keep his person safe must either play the fool to win trust or use wit to escape harm; only when heart and conduct meet no obstruction does he enjoy favor.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: In settled ages a fighting man who means to keep his skin must either seem dull enough to be trusted or sharp enough to slip away—only when mind and deed raise no bar does he win easy grace.

sentences.zh: 崇祖恨結東朝，敬兒情疑鳥盡，嗣運方初，委骨嚴憲。

translations.literal: Chongzu's hatred was fixed with the eastern court; Jing'er's heart suspected the birds were all gone—the successor fortune had only just begun, yet their bones were laid under stern law.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzu's grudge was knotted with the eastern court; Jing'er's heart read the proverb of birds spent and bow stowed—the new reign had barely opened, yet their bones were given to harsh law.

sentences.zh: 若情非發憤，事無感激，功名之閒，不足爲也。

translations.literal: Unless feeling springs from anger rather than gratitude, there is little worth in such acts amid fame and reward.
translations.idiomatic: If the heart is not moved by outrage but by reward, then between fame and gain such deeds are hardly worth the name.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：崇祖爲將，志懷馳逐。

translations.literal: In praise: Chongzu as general, his mind raced to chase the foe.
translations.idiomatic: In praise: Chongzu the commander—his will lived in the gallop after enemies.

sentences.zh: 規搔淮部，立勳豫牧。

translations.literal: He meant to scour the Huai districts and set merit as governor of Yu.
translations.idiomatic: He plotted to rake the Huai country and raise his fame as lord of Yu.

sentences.zh: 敬兒莅雍，深心防楚。

translations.literal: Jing'er ruled Yong, his heart ever wary of Chu.
translations.idiomatic: Jing'er held Yong, his inmost thought a wall against Chu.

sentences.zh: 豈不劬勞，實興師旅。

translations.literal: Was it not toil? In truth he stirred armies.
translations.idiomatic: Was it not labor? In truth he set armies marching.

sentences.zh: 烹犬藏弓，同歸異緒。

translations.literal: Boil the dog and hide the bow—one end, divergent fates.
translations.idiomatic: Cook the hound and stash the bow—one road home, two threads of fate.

sentences.zh: 「賴原卽大世」，疑。

translations.literal: "Lai yuan ji da shi"—doubtful.
translations.idiomatic: "Lai yuan ji da shi"—doubtful reading.

sentences.zh: 案

translations.literal: Note
translations.idiomatic: Note
